title: Video Accessibility: Captions & Beyond 🎬
description: Add captions, subtitles, and audio descriptions to video using WebVTT and accessible players.

slides.title: The Video Accessibility Trio 🎞️
slides.content:
Video needs three things to be fully accessible:

1. **Captions** – synchronised text of all audio (for deaf/hard of hearing).
2. **Audio description** – narration of visual details (for blind/low vision).
3. **Transcript** – full text alternative.

WCAG A requires captions for prerecorded video; AA requires audio descriptions. AAA requires sign language (rarely done).

quizData.question: What is the minimum WCAG level that requires captions for prerecorded video?

slides.title: Captions: Open vs. Closed 📝
slides.content:
* **Closed captions** – can be toggled on/off; stored in a separate file (WebVTT).
* **Open captions** – burned into the video; always visible.

WebVTT is the standard format for captions, subtitles, and descriptions. It's a simple text file with timestamps.

Use the `<track>` element to associate a VTT file with a `<video>`: `<track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">`.

slides.title: VTT File Example
slides.codeSnippet:
WEBVTT

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:10.000
Welcome to our tutorial on accessibility.

00:00:10.500 --> 00:00:14.000
Today we'll cover captions.

quizData.question: Which HTML element do you use to link a captions file to a video?

slides.title: Audio Descriptions 🗣️
slides.content:
Audio description is an additional narration track describing visual information (scene changes, actions, on‑screen text) between dialogue.

* Primary method: a secondary audio track (or a separate described video).
* `<track kind="descriptions" src="desc.vtt">` (for text‑based descriptions read by screen readers – not yet widely supported).
* Better: offer a second version of the video with burned‑in audio description.

If no audio description, provide a text description of the video's visual content alongside it.

quizData.question: What does an audio description provide?

options.text: Narration of visual elements for blind users

quizData.explanation: It describes what is happening visually so that blind users can follow the story.

slides.title: Subtitles vs. Captions 🌍
slides.content:
* **Subtitles** translate dialogue into another language – assume the viewer can hear sound effects.
* **Captions** include dialogue plus important sound effects and speaker identification.

Always use `kind="captions"` for accessibility; `kind="subtitles"` is for language translation.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Don't rely on auto‑generated captions alone
YouTube's auto‑captions are a good start, but they need manual editing for accuracy, punctuation, and speaker labels.
